nodes.name: Clean & Reshape Rows
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Normalize incoming document records to a stable schema Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Rows Pass Validation?
nodes.notes: Two-way gate on ={{ $json.documentId }}. TRUE continues the happy path, FALSE takes the alternate branch. Watch out: The false branch carries the non-matching items — wire it deliberately rather than leaving it dangling.

nodes.name: Quarantine Bad Rows
nodes.notes: Runs a parameterized SQL statement against Postgres — values are bound via queryReplacement, not string-interpolated, so it's immune to SQL injection. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Postgres connection. nodes.name: Save Execution Metadata

nodes.name: Guard Non-Empty fileName
nodes.notes: Drops items that fail the condition; only qualifying items continue (no false branch).

nodes.name: Cap Batch Volume
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 100 items to protect downstream quotas.

nodes.name: Stamp Processing Time
nodes.notes: Stamps processedAt with the current time for auditing.

nodes.notes: Normalizes field names so every source feeds the same downstream schema.

nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes pipeline, version. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Sort Documents Newest First
nodes.notes: Orders items (newest first) so limits and digests pick the most relevant records.

# Parse documents: PostgreSQL

**Pattern:** File Processing · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers invoices work end to end across PostgreSQL, Slack and Google Drive.

It moves through 17 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. Hourly Schedule
2. Download from Google Drive
3. Parse PDF Contents
4. Clean & Reshape Rows
5. Rows Pass Validation?
6. Quarantine Bad Rows
7. Load Rows into PostgreSQL
8. Save Execution Metadata
9. Guard Non-Empty fileName
10. Cap Batch Volume
11. Stamp Processing Time
12. Align Field Names
13. Tag Pipeline Metadata
14. Sort Documents Newest First
15. Summarize Run Stats
16. Append Audit Row (PostgreSQL)
17. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing invoices work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Hourly Schedule → Download from Google Drive → Parse PDF Contents → Clean & Reshape Rows → Rows Pass Validation? → Quarantine Bad Rows → Load Rows into PostgreSQL → Save Execution Metadata → Guard Non-Empty fileName → Cap Batch Volume → Stamp Processing Time → Align Field Names → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Sort Documents Newest First → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (PostgreSQL) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack

## Use it for

- Teams keeping PostgreSQL and Slack aligned by hand for invoices
- Invoices work where "Download from Google Drive" is still a manual step before PostgreSQL
- Invoices work that only reaches PostgreSQL on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps PostgreSQL and Slack in step for invoices, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed PostgreSQL or Slack call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 19 nodes in this invoices build
- Every invoices run leaves an audit row behind, alongside PostgreSQL
- Fans the same result out to Google Drive in the same run, for invoices
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 19 nodes for invoices before wiring PostgreSQL

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2; Postgres connection; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Bad rows are quarantined into their own store, not dropped silently and not allowed to break the whole batch — one malformed row in a 10,000-row file shouldn't stop the other 9,999 from loading, but it also shouldn't vanish without a trace.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Feed it a file with a few deliberately malformed rows and confirm they land in quarantine, not the main store.
2. Switch the source format (e.g. csv to xlsx) and see how little actually has to change.
3. Turn on archive mode and confirm the processed file gets repacked and stored.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Drive API → OAuth2 client or Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Service Accounts have their own empty Drive — share the target folder with it.

**Postgres connection**
Host, port, database, user, password from your Postgres provider.
_Gotcha:_ Managed providers usually require SSL enabled in the credential's options.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Database node cannot connect**
Cause: SSL not enabled, or the n8n server's IP is not allow-listed.
Fix: Most managed database providers require both.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your invoices process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- PostgreSQL: connect as a role that can reach only the tables below, not as the owner.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Google Drive: scope the credential to the one folder this workflow writes to, not `drive.readonly` across the account.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole invoices payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
